## TL;DR

The current macOS Hub QA work verifies building and launching the app, first-run rendering, server discovery and connection, and rendering of the sign-in page. The XCTest registry isolation fix and its cleanup tests are included. Signed-in Projects and Tasks remain unverified because the email-code flow was not completed; human task #1174 still needs results. This draft describes the current source tree and will be finalized by RepoOS after the requested check succeeds.

## Work and rationale

Built the macOS Hub with Xcode using `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` and a task-specific DerivedData location. Launched through LaunchServices with an isolated support directory. The QA record describes the initial empty state, discovery and health checking of a local RepoOS server, persistence of the healthy server entry, and rendering of the sign-in page. Only app-window captures were used.

The QA run exposed that an XCTest app host could write into the developer's normal Hub registry if no support-directory override was set. The app now resolves an explicit override first and uses unique temporary storage for XCTest otherwise. It removes that scratch directory on test-host termination, reports cleanup errors, and tests both cleanup and error propagation. The QA record retains the details of the earlier registry write and its unknown previous selection rather than claiming restoration.

## Approaches tried

Used a dedicated DerivedData path and isolated support storage for the app launch, then inspected the native Hub window and accessibility tree while exercising first-run and add-server flows. A healthy local connection displayed the sign-in page. A direct executable launch showed no content window during the observation interval; this remains an unexplained edge case. Automated email-code interaction did not reach authenticated pages. Stored engineering and review reports are RepoOS-owned and were not edited by hand.

## Challenges and blockers

The Projects and Tasks views require a human to complete the authorized email-code sign-in and record both results in #1174. That task remains human-assigned without results, and the app remains at the code-entry screen. This report does not claim the authenticated acceptance criterion is complete. The requested full `repoos check` is being run against this source before handoff.

## Key learnings

A sign-in page rendering proves connection and web content rendering, not authenticated functionality. The signed-in views need actual observations recorded by the human follow-up. XCTest app-host processes require isolated storage to protect developer data, and cleanup errors should remain visible. RepoOS finalizes engineering reports from a checked commit, so this narrative draft must be present at each handoff.
